      "observations": [
        "All owned hunks in the 16 selected handwritten API/schema, locale, loader, HTML, manifest and token-bridge paths were read. The 31-path import remains incomplete: other owned generated JavaScript is unread and generated CSS ownership is unresolved. Map/image identities are metadata only. The exact compact mapping and read-boundary ledgers preserve these limits; no full-import or whole-bundle audit is claimed.",
        "The original broad bridge injection, commented page-message guards and inspected background message receiver differ from the accepted scoped origins and active source/origin checks. The accepted existing-session guard is a separate later state. The pending-token branch replies by sender tab ID; the telemetry prefix guard belongs to another case and is not a general receiver guard. These facts are static and do not establish an exploit or runtime security result.",
        "Original AccountHub uses server.hostName and forwards getRefreshToken without await despite the same-revision method being async and the event schema requiring a string. Accepted AccountHub uses server.hostname, an async listener and await. The storage-order comment does not remove the promise boundary. Existing focused async-token knowledge is linked rather than generalized into a new rule.",
        "The inspected CloudFileAccounts and MailAccounts APIs create structured results and explicit account/provider state. MailAccounts builds IMAP/SMTP OAuth configuration and awaits backend creation. ProTweaks installs account/provider listeners and an icon override; TBProMenu owns injected nodes and window listeners. The actual generated menu caller uses clear on its root, so a hypothetical root-remove failure is not claimed. No changed tests or executed account, network, clipboard, UI, accessibility or lint result is supplied.",
        "Complete shared primary 0–16, activity/end and full own D298180 creation-to-final timeline were read once. Initial planned hold, first landing, reported lint/network failures, exact backouts, later reland/child update and branch approval phases remain separate. The review has no actual inlines or summary edits. Primary comment 10 rejects disabling lint. External jobs, attachments and upstream feature-flag/XPIProvider bodies remain bounded unread dependencies.",
        "The inspected original sharing implementations use a hardcoded https://send.tb.pro/share URL. The accepted Sharer.requestAccessLink uses config.sendClientUrl. The configuration value and complete caller chain are not established by this comparison.",
        "Both inspected phases generate a password when the supplied string is empty and append that generated value as a URL fragment. These wrappers do not append an explicitly supplied password.",
        "The original index-Bpbldbqs.js exports its W sharingManager store under useMetricsStore. The accepted inspected sharingManager defineStore call has no result binding. This comparison does not prove a wrong consumer or runtime failure; complete dynamic imports and store consumers remain unread.",
        "Challenge failure returns null in the helper; the store increments the password retry count on a missing unwrapped key. Key, network and crypto operations were not executed.",
        "Original qa returns true without consulting a client-only global. Zu searches the compiled https://send.tb.pro string for production, staging and localhost. The accepted clientConfig region uses config.appEnv instead; the config object construction is not covered by this section.",
        "Original config-store starts with https://send-backend.tb.pro, exposes a mutable server URL and chooses an add-on ID by its substring. The accepted counterpart starts from config.sendServerUrl, prefers browser.runtime.id with an ext- prefix, and retains the URL fallback. Original openManagementPage awaits browser.runtime.openOptionsPage with an error catch; the accepted function body is empty.",
        "Both stream helpers first try native pipeThrough and fall back to an explicit reader. In the fallback, pull reads until a transformed value enqueues data; end-of-stream calls optional flush before closing. The accepted fallback adds an optional oncancel callback after readable.cancel. The successful native pipeThrough return does not call that third callback in this function.",
        "Both BlobStreamController variants advance their index when starting FileReader. The onload handler resolves only when the result is an ArrayBuffer; the error handler rejects. No malformed FileReader result or stream cancellation was executed.",
        "Both inspected ECE implementations use a stream slicer, one-record lookbehind, final/nonfinal padding delimiters, a 21-byte header and a key-derived nonce base with a bounded sequence number. Decryption reads the header before decrypting subsequent records. Salt is stored in the header, while the inspected nonce-base function exports the supplied key. This source trace is not a cryptographic safety or interoperability result.",
        "The original init loads user and keychain, synchronizes folders, deletes a default folder whose key is absent, and creates a replacement when absent or orphaned. The accepted init first attempts key restoration, then checks keychain.locked before deleting or creating, uses default-folder lock helpers, and coalesces concurrent init calls through an inFlight promise. The lock and key-restoration helper implementations are not yet inspected in this section.",
        "The accepted initialization enum adds KEYCHAIN_LOCKED. Existing NONE, NO_USER, NO_KEYCHAIN and COULD_NOT_CREATE_DEFAULT_FOLDER values remain distinct. Complete caller handling of the new code remains outside this section.",
        "The original module constructs a WebSocket client from a fixed Send backend URL during module evaluation. The accepted module constructs configuration from config.sendServerUrl, returns no WebSocket configuration for testing or an empty URL, and passes lazy.enabled plus closeMs to the imported client factory. The imported factory implementation and actual connection timing remain unpaired.",
        "Both retry callbacks start a refresh fetch without awaiting its completion, return false for unauthorized non-query operations, and compare attempts with 3 for unauthorized queries. Other error paths return undefined. The broader retry prose is not proof of third-party default behavior or successful token renewal.",
        "The accepted HTTP wrapper builds an Authorization header from getAccessToken when absent, includes credentials, and attempts recovery on x-logout before one repeated fetch. Its auth-store receiver will be inspected in the later background section.",
        "Both retry-until-success helpers wait before calling the predicate, catch predicate errors and return undefined both after success and after exhausting the loop. No timeout or failure was executed.",
        "The original zip wrapper uses JSZip.generateAsync with blob output, while the accepted wrapper consumes generateInternalStream uint8array data and assembles a Blob from chunks. The accepted streamZippedParts helper reads sequential windows, hashes/checks each window and yields zipped parts, then releases its reader lock. Imported JSZip internals and byte-for-byte archive equivalence were not independently checked.",
        "The original filesync layer supports direct server/WebSocket transfer as well as signed bucket URLs. Its Downloader chooses via api.isBucketStorage. The accepted helpers/filesync/Downloader counterpart shown here uses signed bucket transfer only; the old WebSocket upload and connection/message helpers are absent from those inspected component regions.",
        "The original PUT helper materializes a stream as a Blob, retries twice after the initial request with a fixed 1-second delay, and uses a 30-second XHR timeout. The accepted helper still materializes a Blob, but takes an AbortSignal, cleans up abort listeners on load/error/timeout/abort, does not retry an abort, and reads retry defaults from config with jittered exponential delays and a 180-second XHR timeout.",
        "Both encrypt helpers catch errors, log them, and return undefined on that path. The inspected sendBlob callers await the helper then enqueue its result without a distinct success-result check. This is a static error-result contract trace, not an executed upload failure or proof of a network body.",
        "The accepted sendBlob adds size to the signed-upload request, reports the acquired upload ID to an optional callback, propagates the signal to uploadWithTracker, and retains the original error as cause when wrapping UPLOAD_FAILED.",
        "Both file-save functions create and click a download anchor, remove it and revoke the object URL on a zero-delay timer. Their returned promise settles after that cleanup, not after an independently observed completed disk write. The streaming variant attempts showSaveFilePicker before a Blob fallback. No browser save, dialog or filesystem operation was run.",
        "Both Downloader implementations reject reported suspicious uploads before the inner catch, fetch metadata and unwrap a folder content key, then return false for caught download/save failures and record metrics after getBlob resolves. Successful return is this code path, not an independent decryption, integrity or disk verification.",
        "The original Uploader hashes all pieces, prepares all split ZIP blobs and uploads batches of at most five through Promise.all. Its five-attempt loop repeats sendBlob, upload-entry creation and item insertion together; no sibling cancellation or cleanup is shown in that original loop.",
        "The accepted Uploader produces split ZIP parts sequentially into per-part readiness promises, runs at most four workers, drops each consumed part reference, and separates sendBlob from the upload-entry/item retry loop. The entry loop preserves an already-created upload object when retrying item insertion.",
        "The accepted code records acquired upload IDs, passes a shared AbortSignal into sendBlob, aborts workers on a fatal error, attempts uploads/cleanup after the workers finish, and installs a pagehide best-effort cleanup request. The pagehide promise is not awaited and the producer generator does not receive that signal in the inspected call. This is not a proof that every concurrent action or server-side write is stopped or cleaned up.",
        "The accepted code awaits retryUntilSuccessOrTimeout before creating the upload entry. Section 03 establishes that this helper returns undefined after either success or exhaustion, so this await alone does not establish that the stat predicate succeeded.",
        "Both inspected Uploader phases create one content key before iterating the parts and pass that same key to each part upload. Section 02 shows each encryption transformer resets its sequence and derives its nonce base from the supplied key. Key generation/wrapping and actual part receivers are pending the keychain section; no cryptographic safety, exploit or severity claim is made.",
        "The accepted create-entry callback retains structured HTTP/network failure data and reports a cause. A later max-attempt error is a separate wrapper, and historical error-reporting comments do not prove an independently captured production failure.",
        "The original Api constructor normalizes its server URL to an origin and starts an unawaited storage-type query, assigning isBucketStorage later. The inspected accepted constructor retains origin normalization but no longer starts that query or assigns that field; the component callers read in Sections 04 and 05 use signed bucket transfer directly.",
        "Both call methods add /api/ before the supplied path, add a bearer token when absent if available, include cookies and serialize a body only for POST. Initial network failures and some refresh failures return null; success returns the raw response when requested or the JSON promise. URL construction and response JSON errors are not inside those network catches, so a blanket never-rejects/null-only contract would be false.",
        "The accepted buildApiUrl rejects empty, authority/scheme, backslash and dot-segment paths, then checks origin and /api/ pathname. The accepted call handles x-logout through the auth receiver, adds structured failure callbacks and a bounded Retry-After retry for 429. These are exact client-side source checks, not an independent server-request security result.",
        "Both removeAuthToken methods pass api/auth/oidc/logout to call even though call itself adds the /api/ prefix. The concrete caller reachability is pending the auth-store section; no observed logout failure is claimed here.",
        "Both storage adapters JSON-serialize values in localStorage and clear the entire adapter through localStorage.clear. The accepted Storage adds clearKeys, removing only lb/keys and lb/passphrase while retaining other stored entries; keychain/auth callers remain the later source boundary.",
        "Both content-key generators request an exportable 256-bit AES-GCM key. Both container-key implementations request AES-KW and wrap/unwrap content keys. Password wrapping derives an AES-KW key from PBKDF2 with the supplied salt and 100000 iterations. This records exact inputs and algorithm names; it does not certify cryptographic safety or native API behavior.",
        "Combined with Sections 02 and 05, the source uses one content key for all upload parts, creates a new ECE transformer per part with sequence zero, and derives each nonce base from the first 12 raw bytes of that same key. The per-transformer salt is written to the header but is not an input to the inspected nonce-base calculation. This is a static same-input/sequence trace, with no runtime, exploit or severity claim.",
        "Both backup orchestrators generate one backup key and one salt, then pass that same key and salt to encryption of the public key, private key and each stored container-key string. Backup.encryptBackup passes the supplied salt as the AES-GCM iv. The source-level key/IV identity is explicit in both phases; no backup or attack was executed.",
        "The original restore locks the keychain for any error in the decryption/load/store block. The accepted decryptAll wraps only password-key unwrapping errors in IncorrectPassphraseError; accepted restore coalesces per-keychain calls, locks only that typed error, clears the lock on its success path and rethrows other errors without locking.",
        "Both restore paths await keychain.load and then keychain.store without checking the boolean returned by load. Keychain.load catches its import/load errors and returns false. Therefore the caller reaching its Restore complete label does not by itself establish that load returned true. No malformed key material was supplied.",
        "Both backup paths await the create-backup API helper and then set Backup complete without checking its returned value. Section 06 establishes that some API failures return null. The label therefore does not by itself establish a successful backup response; no network failure was reproduced.",
        "Both keychain stores retain one Keychain instance and delegate add/get/remove/new-key operations to it. resetKeychain calls _init on that instance; _init resets key objects and storage but does not assign locked. The constructor assigns locked separately. Complete reset/logout callers are pending the auth section.",
        "Both user stores copy backend/user fields into a reactive object, read/store the same user storage keys, and populate users/me only when user.id is absent. The default reset iterates only id, tier, email and thundermailEmail. Additional populated fields such as name and uniqueHash are not deleted by that loop. Consumer impact is not inferred here.",
        "Both getPublicKey/updatePublicKey methods dereference the result of Api.call before a root null guard; update guards only the update property. Section 06 establishes possible null API failure returns. No network failure or resulting exception was executed.",
        "Both folder-view helpers keep nonmultipart items and represent a multipart item only when upload.part equals 1, replacing its displayed upload.size with totalSize. They return a new array. Complete multipart download and UI consumers remain the next folder-store section; this is not a claim that all parts are read or joined here.",
        "The accepted message catalog adds cookie/storage and app-load retry guidance. These strings are source declarations, not independently verified settings, recovery or accessibility outcomes.",
        "Both metrics stores retain a PostHog receiver and call identify only when an ID is truthy. The accepted plugin also installs a globalProperties receiver. Imported analytics internals and event transmission remain unread and unexecuted.",
        "Both token validators obtain an access token before the optional loadUser call, try the OIDC me endpoint, try refresh if necessary, then fall back to a legacy auth/me request. This section records ordering only; the auth-store methods remain the next component.",
        "Both validators set hasCorrectKeys true after restoreKeysUsingLocalStorage resolves. Section 07 shows that the helper can return early for a missing passphrase or unavailable backup, and that restore ignores Keychain.load returning false. A resolved restore call is therefore not a boolean proof that keys were loaded or validated.",
        "The original validator requests clearing storage after any restore exception or a backend/local user-ID mismatch. The accepted counterpart separates a locked keychain: it calls clearBridgedPassphrase instead of marking that branch for storage clearing. Other errors and explicit user-ID mismatch still lead to clearUserFromStorage and a reload request. The bridge-helper implementation is outside this section.",
        "The backed-up-keys predicate checks for both a truthy backup response and a nonempty stored passphrase; it does not decrypt or compare the backup itself. No profile, authentication or restore result was executed.",
        "Both status stores keep progress state, call an imported debounce helper, clamp percentage above 100 and replace NaN with zero. They expose the validator inspected in Section 09. Imported debounce timing and rendered progress behavior are not established here.",
        "The original default folder is the final array entry. The accepted selectDefaultFolder scans backward for an entry with a stored key and otherwise uses the final entry. The source does not itself sort folders or establish chronological newest order. Accepted fetchSubtree distinguishes locked-keychain 403 with a typed error and refreshes the root list after certain 403/404 responses.",
        "Both createFolder paths create a container, add a key, attempt backup/storage and roll back the container on a thrown error. Accepted createFolder skips backup when locked. Because the backup helper can resolve after a null API response, reaching this path is not proof of a server-side backup; rollback API null results are also not checked.",
        "The actual uploadItem caller treats the helper named canUserUpload as an exceeded-limit predicate: it throws when the returned total-plus-size comparison is true. This resolves the naming/receiver boundary from Section 03 without changing the observed arithmetic. Accepted uploadItem additionally tries to populate a missing user ID before upload.",
        "Both deleteItem functions pass { shouldDeleteContent: true } with method DELETE to Api.call. Section 06 shows that call attaches a JSON body only for POST. Therefore these exact wrapper paths do not serialize that argument into a DELETE request body. Backend defaults, actual deletion and data loss are not established.",
        "Both multipart download paths fetch all part metadata concurrently, sort part numbers, then process parts sequentially with the same unwrapped content key. Each piece buffers its decrypted chunks into a Uint8Array before unzipping; an async ReadableStream start loop enqueues each resulting piece. The accepted comment gives numerical peak-memory estimates, but this code and the Blob fallback in Section 04 do not establish those measurements or a hard memory bound.",
        "The returned folder/file views apply organizeFiles inside computed wrappers. That caller establishes the plain array helper from Section 08 as a presentation transform, while downloadMultipart separately fetches every part. Hidden representative parts are not treated as absent download bytes.",
        "Both handleOIDCCallback and authenticateWithAddonToken pass an object containing method: POST and headers as the second argument to Api.call. Section 06 establishes that the second positional argument is body, the third defaults to GET, and only a POST method serializes body. Those exact caller objects do not select POST or supply the wrapper headers argument. The wrapper may separately obtain a bearer token. No backend method requirement, actual request or authentication failure was tested.",
        "The original auth settings use fixed authority/client values, automaticSilentRenew true and loadUserInfo true. The accepted settings read configured authority/client values and set the latter two flags false. The imported OIDC implementation and provider-side behavior remain unpaired.",
        "Accepted refreshAccessToken coalesces concurrent refreshes, stores a returned extension user, and clears local state only for a listed string error code. recoverOrForceLogout attempts that refresh and invokes forced logout only after a listed genuine failure. The exact API callers from Section 06 retry only when that method returns true; there is no runtime recovery guarantee.",
        "Actual logoutFromOIDC calls auth/oidc/logout with an explicit third-argument POST and then signoutRedirect.
